<Aside type="note" title="Build mechanism changed (WI-5651) — this testing recipe is about the VM as a TEST target, not a build machine">
This doc predates WI-5651, which retired the VM as the Windows **build**
mechanism. Builds now use `papercusp-desktop/bin/build-windows-cross.sh`,
cross-compiled on Linux. Nothing here is about building, though — it's about
driving an *installed* Windows app inside a VM for a first-run smoke test, and
that need doesn't go away just because the artifact is no longer built inside
that same VM: a Windows box (VM or otherwise) is still needed to install and
run whatever `papercusp-desktop/bin/build-windows-cross.sh` produces. The SSH/SPICE/scheduled-task
recipe below should still apply to a cross-built installer, but has not been
specifically re-verified against one.
</Aside>

The Windows 11 dev VM (`~/windows-vm/`, QEMU; **ssh `-p 2223 user@127.0.0.1`**
key `~/.ssh/papercup-vm-win`, **SPICE `:5931`**, HMP monitor at
`~/windows-vm/qemu-monitor.sock`) is normally driven by a human at a `spicy`
viewer. You do **not** need one — a full first-run GUI smoke is drivable
headlessly. This is how WI-800 (the 0.0.2 alpha first-run smoke) was done.

<Aside type="caution" title="SSH lands in a NON-visible session">
OpenSSH on this VM authenticates into a session that is **not** the interactive
console (session 1). A GUI launched with `Start-Process` from your SSH
PowerShell renders on an invisible window station — `screendump` shows nothing
and `MainWindowHandle` is 0. To put a window on the SPICE console (or to inject
input there) you must run **in session 1**, which you reach with an
**interactive scheduled task** (`schtasks /it`). This is the single biggest
gotcha.
</Aside>

## The four primitives

1. **PowerShell over SSH without quoting hell** — `cmd` mangles `$`. Encode the
   script UTF-16LE→base64 and run `powershell -EncodedCommand`:
   ```bash
   B64="$(printf '%s' "$SCRIPT" | iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-16LE | base64 -w0)"
   ssh -i ~/.ssh/papercup-vm-win -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -p 2223 user@127.0.0.1 \
     "powershell -NoProfile -EncodedCommand $B64"
   ```
   `-o IdentitiesOnly=yes` is required — a loaded ssh-agent with >5 keys trips
   "Too many authentication failures" before the `-i` key is tried.

2. **Observe the screen** — QEMU monitor `screendump` writes the framebuffer to
   PPM; convert with `pnmtopng`:
   ```bash
   printf 'screendump /tmp/s.ppm\n' | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:~/windows-vm/qemu-monitor.sock
   pnmtopng /tmp/s.ppm > /tmp/s.png   # ~200 bytes ⇒ black/asleep; wake with `sendkey shift`
   ```
   Crop with ImageMagick (`convert s.png -crop WxH+X+Y +repage out.png`) to read
   button labels and derive pixel coordinates (the framebuffer is 1280×800).

3. **Launch the GUI on the visible console (session 1)** — an interactive task:
   ```
   schtasks /create /tn t /tr "<exe-or-wrapper>" /sc once /st 00:00 /it /rl LIMITED /f
   schtasks /run /tn t
   ```
   Use `/rl LIMITED` (non-elevated = the real double-click path). Wrap the exe in
   a `.cmd` that `set RUST_LOG=info,papercusp=debug` and redirects stdout to a
   file to capture the Tauri/sidecar boot log (read it back with a
   FileShare.ReadWrite open — the running app keeps the handle).

4. **Inject mouse clicks into session 1** — a tiny `SetCursorPos` +
   `mouse_event(0x2/0x4)` PS script, run via an interactive task at the pixel
   coords you read from the screenshot. (QEMU HMP `mouse_move` is relative and
   unreliable with `usb-tablet`; `sendkey` works for keyboard but Win32 cursor
   injection in-session is the robust way to click.)

## Clean-reset recipe (for a genuine *first*-run)

```powershell
Get-Process papercusp-desktop | Stop-Process -Force
& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Papercusp\uninstall.exe" /S            # NSIS (per-user)
Start-Process msiexec -ArgumentList '/X{GUID}','/quiet' -Wait # any old MSI install
wsl --unregister papercup-runtime                            # force re-import next boot
Remove-Item "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\com.papercusp.desktop","$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Papercusp" -Recurse -Force
```

## What a healthy first-run looks like

- `wsl -l -v` shows `papercup-runtime` re-import → **Running**.
- Inside the distro: `postgres -D /home/papercup/.papercusp/embedded-pg-data`
  and `node … serve.mjs --ensure` running; the PG port forwards to Windows
  `127.0.0.1`.
- Tauri stdout: `[serve] listening on http://127.0.0.1:<port> (UI ON)`,
  `/api/health` → 200, `DBOS launched`.
- The dogfood clone **defers gracefully** with no GitHub auth:
  `[papercusp-pot] not created this boot: clone auth_required: awaiting GitHub sign-in`
  (never a crash/trap). The `DogfoodBootstrapBanner` is dismissible.

## Gotchas

- **Elevated launch ⇒ no window.** `schtasks /rl HIGHEST` (elevated) boots the
  backend fine but the Tauri webview window never appears (`MainWindowHandle`
  stays 0). Use `/rl LIMITED`. Users double-click non-elevated, so this is a
  test artifact, not a public bug — but it will waste an hour if you don't know it.
- **First-run self-restart.** After the WSL import the app relaunches itself
  (the PID changes) to spawn the sidecar through the freshly-set-up `wsl.exe` —
  expected (see `main.rs` / `wsl_setup.rs`).
- **Spaces-in-username** is testable without switching console users: create a
  `First Last` account, grant `SeBatchLogonRight` (secedit), then install + launch
  the app via a task `/ru "First Last"`. The startup log proves all Windows-side
  paths resolve with the space (`shared sidecar home: C:\Users\First Last`,
  `\\?\C:\Users\First Last\…`). The operator boot under the spaces profile needs
  interactive onboarding (a fresh user has no distro), so it's a partial test.
- **SmartScreen is NOT exercised by an scp'd installer** — it has no Mark-of-the-Web.
  Testing the "unknown publisher" wall needs a real browser download (and is moot
  once the installer is Authenticode-signed).
